argument: Party A says childhood vaccines cause autism and that's why they won't vaccinate their kid. Party B says that study was retracted and vaccines are safe. Party A says big pharma hides the truth.
Party A insists goldfish only have a 3-second memory so keeping one in a small bowl is fine. Party B says goldfish can actually remember things for months and need proper tanks.
My dad says cracking my knuckles will give me arthritis when I'm older and I need to stop. I say that's a myth and studies show no connection. He says everyone knows it's true.
Party A bet Party B $50 that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye. Party B says astronauts themselves have said you can't see it from orbit without aid.
Party A won't let the kids have cake at the party because sugar makes children hyperactive. Party B says controlled studies show the sugar-hyperactivity link is a myth and it's just party excitement.
Party A says you must wear a hat because you lose most of your body heat through your head. Party B says that's an old myth — you lose heat proportionally to exposed surface area.

Party A refuses to shelter under the tower because lightning never strikes the same place twice, so the field is safer since it was hit last year. Party B says tall structures get struck repeatedly all the time.
Party A says bulls charge at the matador's cape because the color red enrages them. Party B says bulls are colorblind to red and react to the movement of the cape.
Party A argues: everyone who cheats ends up winning, our rival won the tournament, therefore they must have cheated. Party B says winning doesn't prove cheating even if cheaters often win.

Party A says if we let employees work from home one day a week, soon nobody will ever come to the office and the company will collapse, so we can't allow any remote work. Party B says one day a week doesn't lead inevitably to zero office time.

Party A says seatbelts are dangerous because their uncle survived a crash only because he was thrown clear of the car. Party B says statistics across millions of crashes show seatbelts save lives overall.
Party A says the herbal remedy must be safe because it's natural, unlike chemical medicine. Party B points out plenty of natural things are poisonous and 'natural' doesn't mean safe.
Party A says we must keep doing the quarterly report this way because we've always done it this way. Party B says age of a practice alone doesn't make it the best way.

Party B says we should let our 16-year-old sister go to a music festival alone with her friends because she needs freedom to grow up. Party A says it's not safe, she's too young, and safety comes first.

Party A wants security cameras on every street corner because they deter crime and help catch criminals. Party B says mass surveillance destroys privacy and a free society shouldn't watch everyone all the time. Both agree cameras do reduce some crime.
Party A gives 20% of their income to overseas charities and says Party B is selfish for spending on family vacations instead. Party B says taking care of your own family first isn't selfish.

Party A told their friend the haircut looked great when it didn't, to spare feelings. Party B says lying is always wrong and real friends tell the truth. Party A says kindness matters more than blunt honesty.
Party A thinks the inheritance should be split equally between all siblings because equal is fair. Party B thinks the sibling who cared for their sick mother for five years deserves a larger share.

Party A wants to take a lower-paying job doing meaningful nonprofit work. Party B, their spouse, says they have kids and financial security has to come before personal fulfillment. Both agree the pay cut is 30%.
Party A says a hot dog is obviously a sandwich: meat between bread. Party B says nobody who orders a sandwich expects a hot dog, so it isn't one. They've been arguing for an hour.
Party A says chess is a sport because it has competition, rankings, and requires training. Party B says a sport requires physical athleticism, so chess is a game, not a sport.
Party A says a tomato is a fruit, full stop, botany says so. Party B says in cooking and common speech it's a vegetable and that's what matters. They want a ruling.
Party A says sleeping in a tent with no shower isn't a real vacation, vacations mean rest and comfort. Party B says vacation just means time away doing what you love, and they love camping.
Party A says AI-generated images aren't real art because there's no human struggle behind them. Party B says art is whatever moves the viewer, regardless of how it was made.

We can only keep one employee. Party A says keep Jordan: Jordan's sales numbers are double Sam's. Party B says keep Sam: Sam mentors juniors, holds the team together, and Jordan has caused two colleagues to quit. We agree the goal is what's best for the company over five years.

Party A says they do all the cooking so Party B should do all the cleaning. Party B says they work 20 more hours a week outside the home, so splitting home chores 50/50 isn't fair either. Both are exhausted.

Party A lets the kids have tablets at dinner because it keeps things calm and they finish their food. Party B says dinner should be for family conversation even if it's messier. Party A agrees conversation matters; Party B agrees the calm is real.

Party A got a job offer in another city with 40% more pay and wants to move. Party B, their partner, would have to leave a job they love and their aging parents. Party A says the money secures their future; Party B says some things matter more than money. Both numbers are undisputed.

Party A says pre-rinsing dishes before the dishwasher wastes water and modern machines don't need it. Party B says their dishes come out dirty without rinsing. Party A says Party B just loads the machine wrong.

Party A wants to adopt a husky because they're beautiful and the family will exercise more. Party B says they live in a small hot-climate apartment, both work full time, and a husky would be miserable. Party A says love is what matters most for a pet.

PARTY A'S SIDE:
Party A says the moon landings were staged in a studio and the flag only waves because of a fan.

PARTY B'S SIDE:
Party B says the landings happened: the mirrors the crews left on the surface are still used to bounce lasers off the moon, and thousands of people worked on the missions.

PARTY C'S SIDE:
Party C says the landings happened but the official story hides how many missions nearly failed, so nobody should trust the agency about anything.

PARTY A'S SIDE:
Party A stayed all five nights of the group trip and says the villa bill should be split by nights stayed.

PARTY B'S SIDE:
Party B booked the villa for everyone and says it should be split evenly three ways, because nobody asked to pay by the night when they agreed to come.

PARTY C'S SIDE:
Party C only came for two nights because of work and says splitting evenly makes them pay for three nights they were not there, though they will pay their share of the shared food.

PARTY A'S SIDE:
Party A cooked dinner for all three roommates and says whoever did not cook should do the dishes.

PARTY B'S SIDE:
Party B did the dishes the last two times and says it is now Party A's turn, whoever cooked.

PARTY C'S SIDE:
Party C bought the groceries for the dinner and says buying counts as much as cooking, so the dishes should go to Party A or Party B.

PARTY A'S SIDE:
Party A says the team meeting is on Tuesday because that is when it was last month.

PARTY B'S SIDE:
Party B says it is on Wednesday because a colleague told them in the hallway.

PARTY C'S SIDE:
Party C says the calendar invite sent by the manager reads Thursday at 10:00, and the manager has not changed it.

PARTY D'S SIDE:
Party D says they do not remember the day but the room was booked for the whole week, so it does not matter.

PARTY A'S SIDE:
Party A says a hot dog is a sandwich, because it is meat inside bread.

PARTY B'S SIDE:
Party B says a hot dog is not a sandwich, because nobody orders a sandwich and gets a hot dog, and restaurants list them separately.

PARTY C'S SIDE:
Party C says a hot dog is a taco, because it is a single folded bread holding the filling.

PARTY D'S SIDE:
Party D says it is a category of its own and the question is pointless.

PARTY A'S SIDE:
Party A says the team only wins because of its star player, since they won every game he played this season.

PARTY B'S SIDE:
Party B says winning every game he played proves nothing, because he plays the easy home games.

PARTY C'S SIDE:
Party C says the season record shows the team also won all three games he missed, two of them away, so his presence is not what decides results.
